test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 18 Oct, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The basic structure of the Indian Constitution stands on the Government of India Act, ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1935**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Government of India Act, 1935, served as the **foundation for the Indian Constitution**, providing many administrative structures and features.
 
• The Act introduced significant elements like the **federal system, provincial autonomy, and bicameralism**, which were later adopted in the Indian Constitution.
 
• The **Indian Constitution** borrowed key features such as the structure of governance, emergency provisions, and the division of powers from this act.
 
• The Act established an **All-India Federation**, although it was never fully implemented as princely states did not join.
 
• The **Government of India Act, 1935**, is considered the longest and most detailed act of British India, influencing the structure of modern Indian governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Federal Structure:** The Government of India Act, 1935, introduced the concept of a federal structure with powers divided between the Centre and provinces.
 
• **Provincial Autonomy:** The Act granted autonomy to provinces, allowing elected representatives to have more control over local governance.
 
• **Instrument of Instructions:** These were guidelines for the Governor-General and Governors, later incorporated into the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Bicameralism:** The Act introduced bicameral legislatures at the Centre, a feature retained in the Indian Constitution with the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
 
• **Emergency Provisions:** The Act had provisions for emergency powers, which were later adapted and expanded in the Indian Constitution under Articles 352, 356, and 360.
